findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a covering criterion for W1 (gate execution moved off the Gerrit host) OR explicitly mark W1 as superseded by the resize+cap approach in AC3.
evidence: W1: 'Move gate execution off the Gerrit host ... Removes the bursty heavy consumer entirely'
AC3 evidence: 'nene moved host to non-burst r7g.large; ladybug caps gates at 2 and refuses below the memory floor' — no move-off-host artifact
findings.finding: W1 ('Move gate execution off the Gerrit host'), presented as the highest-leverage workstream, has no covering acceptance criterion; the ACs instead resolve gate contention via instance resize + a gate cap of 2 (W3+W4).
scenarios: Reviewer checking whether the leading remediation was actually delivered
findings.suggested_fix: State in Workstreams that W1 was not pursued and AC3 satisfies the contention concern via W3+W4 instead, or add an AC attesting gates now run off-host.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the per-service mem_limit values between child 48f0 (mcp 2048 / review-bot 1280, sum 6656) and child 04dd (mcp 3655 / review-bot 1343, sum 9088) so both children cite one authoritative sizing and one consistent host-fit conclusion.
evidence: 48f0 Changes #2: 'mcp 2048m ... review-bot 1280m ... Sum 6656 MiB = 6.5 GiB, leaving 1.3 GiB (17%) for OS + page cache'
04dd Context: 'gerrit 3072 + mcp 3655 + review-bot 1343 + opcert 256 = 9088 MiB / host total ... 7813 MiB -> OVER by 1275 MiB ... The $0 half is therefore arithmetically unlandable as sized'
48f0 AC2: 'their sum leaving >= 1 GiB free' — i.e. 48f0 asserts its limits DO fit the current host, the direct negation of 04dd's premise that they do not
container pairing: parent + 04dd-b3af-9b3d-4a91/48f0-f7ff-c8df-43ac/5ee6-5523-2a12-46e0
findings.finding: Children 04dd and 48f0 contradict each other on the per-service mem_limit values and on whether those limits fit the un-resized host. 48f0 (as written) sizes mcp=2048m and review-bot=1280m for a sum of 6656 MiB that it claims fits the 7813 MiB host with 1.3 GiB (17%) headroom. 04dd (as written) cites the same ladybug limits as mcp=3655 and review-bot=1343 for a sum of 9088 MiB, and its entire justification is that 9088 > 7813 so the resize is mandatory. The two children give different numbers for the same shared artifact and reach opposite conclusions about host fit.
scenarios: A reviewer reading 48f0 concludes the memory limits already fit a 7813 MiB box (no resize needed); a reviewer reading 04dd concludes they cannot fit and a resize is required — the two plans cannot both be executed as written

If 48f0 lands its 6656 MiB sizing, 04dd's stated justification (9088 MiB overflow) is false, undermining the resize rationale; if 04dd's 9088 MiB sizing is the real one, 48f0's AC2 (sum leaves >= 1 GiB free on the current host) fails
findings.suggested_fix: Single-source the mem_limit values in child 48f0 and have 04dd reference them by pointer rather than restating divergent numbers; state explicitly whether the limits are sized-for-16 GiB (requiring 04dd) or sized-for-8 GiB (making 04dd optional), and align 48f0's AC2 'leaves >= 1 GiB free' with the target host.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile W4 with the delivered mechanism: state that the concurrent-SUM bound is enforced by W2's static per-container mem_limits (+ slot cap 2), and describe the MemAvailable floor as a fail-closed precondition/back-pressure signal rather than a dynamic total-memory reservation — or, if a true reservation is intended, specify how concurrent admissions reserve budget (TOCTOU-safe) rather than each re-reading MemAvailable.
evidence: W4: 'One admission controller aware of total memory ... replacing independent gate semaphore + MCP thread limiter + review-bot concurrency.'
gate_admission.py _require_available_memory docstring: 'This is a precondition, not a reservation'
AC2 evidence tests a single monkeypatched refusal ('MemAvailable=512 MiB and gate_admission refused before work'), not two concurrent admissions each reading above the floor
AC1's actual sum-bound is static: 'docker inspect ceilings are gerrit 3072m, review-bot 2048m, opcert 256m, mcp 3712m' — i.e. W2, not a dynamic total-memory controller
findings.finding: W4 describes 'one admission controller aware of total memory' that 'bounds the SUM', but the delivered/named mechanism is a per-call MemAvailable floor check that is (per its own design) a precondition, not a reservation — so concurrent admissions are not summed, and the real sum-bound comes from W2's static per-container ceilings, not from W4.
findings.location: Workstreams — W4 'Bound the SUM, not the parts'; corroborated by AC1/AC2 evidence and gate_admission._require_available_memory
scenarios: Two plan-review gates admitted within the same MemAvailable sampling window each pass the floor check and both run, pushing concurrent RSS past the intended ceiling — the very 'nothing sums the parts' defect the thesis names
A reader implementing W4 as literally 'a controller aware of total memory' builds a dynamic reservation that the check-then-act code does not actually provide
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite W4 to name the static per-container ceilings as the load-bearing sum-bound and recast the admission floor as 'refuse to START a gate when the host is already in the low-memory band' (a precondition), explicitly noting it does not reserve per-gate budget and therefore is not itself the SUM bound.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the thesis (move tier, do not retune) with AC1/AC3 (resize + cap at 2) by noting the resize changes the memory arithmetic that made retuning unsafe.
evidence: Thesis: 'at current resident usage the box cannot safely run even ONE plan-review gate ... the argument for moving the tier, not retuning it'
AC1/AC3: box resized to r7g.large 15,678 MiB and 'max_concurrent_gates=2' — the very retuning the thesis says is insufficient, now made safe by the resize
findings.finding: The thesis concludes that tuning the semaphore down 'does not reach a safe number — which is the argument for moving the tier, not retuning it', yet AC3 resolves the problem by retuning (capping gates at 2) on a resized host — a cross-section contradiction between the diagnosis and the delivered fix.
scenarios: Implementer reconciling the argued approach against what was shipped
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the thesis or AC3 clarifying that the retune-is-insufficient conclusion applied to the 7.8 GiB box, and the r7g.large resize is what makes a 2-gate cap safe.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the single-admission-controller decision (replacing the three independent limiters) in an ADR/design-doc so the 'bound the SUM' invariant survives future edits.
evidence: 'One admission controller aware of total memory, replacing independent gate semaphore + MCP thread limiter + review-bot concurrency, each locally reasonable.'
No ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update is mentioned for this consolidation.
findings.finding: W4 introduces a new single admission controller that replaces three independent limiters (gate semaphore + MCP thread limiter + review-bot concurrency) — a novel cross-component architectural consolidation — but no ADR/design-doc capture of this decision is planned.
findings.location: Workstreams W4 — 'Bound the SUM, not the parts'
scenarios: A future maintainer re-adds a local limiter, reintroducing the un-summed-ceiling defect the plan is fixing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit, cheap rollback for the container mem-limits and admission-controller cutover (e.g. disable via [snapshot] flip / prior compose) and the deploy ordering relative to the instance resize.
evidence: 'nene moved host to non-burst r7g.large'
docker ceilings declared but no stated way to revert the limits/admission cutover quickly
The only revert discipline in the plan is for alarm widenings ('That revert must be honoured'), not for the host/container changes.
findings.finding: The plan changes runtime behavior of a deployed host (instance-family migration to r7g.large, per-container mem limits, admission-controller cutover) but states no explicit rollback path or deploy ordering for these core changes — only the alarm-widening revert trigger is called out.
scenarios: A mis-sized mem_limit OOM-kills an interactive container repeatedly and the operator has no pre-stated fast revert.
The admission controller mis-rejects legitimate gate work and there is no documented flip-back to the prior limiters.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in W3/AC3 whether the r7g.large family change is an in-place instance_type update or a replacement of aws_instance.gerrit, and cite the data-continuity guarantees (prevent_destroy on aws_ebs_volume.data, EIP survives replacement, ignore_changes=[ami]) so the apply's blast radius is explicit.
evidence: Plan W3: 'Right-size or change instance family... BURSTABLE IS THE WRONG FAMILY'
AC3 evidence: 'nene moved host to non-burst r7g.large'

Terraform makes this safe but implicitly: aws_ebs_volume.data has prevent_destroy, aws_eip.gerrit has prevent_destroy and 'survives instance stop/start and replacement', aws_instance.gerrit has lifecycle ignore_changes=[ami]
The plan text does not itself state the replace-vs-in-place path or data-continuity guarantee
findings.finding: W3 (change instance family) and AC3 assert the Gerrit host was moved to a non-burst r7g.large without stating the change mechanics: whether it is an in-place instance_type attribute update or a force-replacement of aws_instance.gerrit, and how Gerrit site data and the public address survive it.
scenarios: An instance-family change that force-replaces aws_instance.gerrit runs the reattach of the prevent_destroy data volume and EIP; if not planned explicitly the operator may not distinguish a benign in-place resize from a replacement
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to W3 noting the change is an in-place instance_type update on aws_instance.gerrit (or, if a replacement, that the separate prevent_destroy data volume and EIP preserve Gerrit's site and address), verified against the terraform plan diff before apply.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign parent AC6 (re-take measurements after change 2685 deploys) to a specific child's acceptance criteria, or split it into its own child, rather than discharging it solely in an epic comment.
evidence: Parent AC6: 'Measurements were re-taken after change 2685 deployed. Evidence 2026-09-06 comments: ... post-deploy MCP measured 2.87 GiB'
48f0 'Measured basis' uses CloudWatch 48h Avg/Max 2026-09-03T17:00Z-2026-09-05 with mcp max 4.64 GB — a PRE-2685 measurement, not a re-take after deploy
04dd Context cites 'MCP alone measures 2.87 GiB steady state (post-change-2685, recorded on the epic under AC6)' — consuming the figure, not re-taking it
Roster: neither 04dd, 48f0, nor 5ee6 lists an AC whose observable outcome is 're-take and record measurements after 2685 deploys'
container pairing: parent + 04dd-b3af-9b3d-4a91/48f0-f7ff-c8df-43ac/5ee6-5523-2a12-46e0
findings.finding: Parent AC6 ('Measurements were re-taken after change 2685 deployed') is not covered by any sibling's acceptance criteria. No child owns a re-measurement AC: 04dd only references the post-2685 2.87 GiB figure as input, and 48f0's 'Measured basis' table uses PRE-2685 CloudWatch data (mcp max 4.64 GB). AC6 was discharged only in an epic comment, not delegated to a child.
scenarios: A completion verifier walking the roster finds no child AC delivering AC6's observable outcome, so the parent criterion has no child evidence path
The 2685 deploy-and-remeasure was only ever recorded as an epic comment; if that comment is treated as out-of-band, the criterion is structurally unowned
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit AC to child 48f0 (which owns the memory sizing) that the mem_limit sizing basis is a post-2685-deploy measurement, and record the re-take there; or file a dedicated measurement child.
